chunks: Hadith 5572 — Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad narrated from ʿUmar ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar, from Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad al-Hamadhānī, who said:

I wrote to him, peace be upon him, about a deceased person who had made a bequest that what remained of his one-third be spent on a man, but he did not instruct that his entire one-third be executed. Does the executor have the right to make the deceased’s one-third into an endowment because of this ongoing expenditure?
So he, peace be upon him, wrote: “His one-third is to be carried out, and it is not to be made into an endowment.”

key_terms.الْوَصِيِّ: the executor entrusted with carrying out the will
key_terms.ثُلُثِهِ: his one-third share of the estate that may be disposed of by will
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: a deceased person whose estate and bequest are under discussion
key_terms.يُنْفِذُ: to execute or carry out the bequest
key_terms.يُوقِفَ: to make into an endowment or waqf

ai.seo_question: Can an executor turn a deceased person’s one-third bequest into an endowment if the will only mentions ongoing support?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the execution of a deceased person’s bequest from the one-third portion of the estate. The Imam عليه السلام states that the will should be carried out according to what was specified, but the executor may not convert that one-third into a waqf/endowment when the deceased did not explicitly instruct that.
